questions: Should the column indexes in remove_cols refer to positions in the original columns list before any removal, or to positions in the DataFrame as it is being built (i.e., after previous removals if multiple indexes are given)?
If remove_cols contains duplicate indexes, should the function ignore duplicates, raise an error, or attempt removal multiple times (which would cause an error)?
Should the function validate that all indexes in remove_cols are within the valid range of column indices (0 to len(columns)-1) and raise an error if not, or silently ignore out-of-range indices?
If remove_cols is an empty list, should the function return a DataFrame with all original columns unchanged?
Should the random integer values be inclusive of both 0 and 100 (i.e., [0, 100]) or exclusive of 100 (i.e., [0, 100))?
If n_rows is 0, should the function still generate a DataFrame with zero rows but with the remaining columns (after removal) as empty columns?
Should the function ensure that the columns parameter is a list of unique strings, or can it handle duplicate column names?
If random_seed is None, should the function use a non-deterministic random state or a default fixed seed?
